verdict.rationale: Keycloak is a standards-based OAuth 2.0/OIDC authorization server. Its docs cover the main building blocks an MCP auth layer needs: discovery via the well-known endpoint, dynamic client registration, client-credentials and device grants for agents, token introspection and revocation for verifying tokens, and fine-grained authorization for scoping. Nothing in the evidence ties these to the MCP authorization spec, so fronting an MCP server is a do-it-yourself integration rather than a documented flow. Missing for 10: MCP-specific guidance or integration docs, evidence of PKCE/resource-indicator (audience-bound token) support, protected-resource metadata support, and independent hands-on corroboration of use with MCP servers.
